```sql
-- name: top_customers
-- owner: sales
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
-- Customers ranked by revenue, with their most recent order. Only customers
-- whose last order falls inside the window are listed.
WITH t AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)           AS order_count,
           max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY o.customer_id
    HAVING max(o.created_at) >= %(from)s
       AND max(o.created_at) <  %(to)s
)
SELECT c.id,
       c.email,
       c.company,
       c.country_code,
       t.revenue,
       t.order_count,
       t.last_order_at
  FROM customers c
  JOIN t ON t.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
 ORDER BY t.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De `DISTINCT ON (customer_id) ... ORDER BY created_at DESC` levert exact `max(created_at)` op (created_at is NOT NULL), dus de twee afgeleide tabellen zijn samengevoegd tot één GROUP BY over orders; daardoor vervalt de dubbele scan van de gematerialiseerde CTE én de rampzalige nested loop tussen `last_order` en `totals` (48 miljoen rijen weggefilterd door de join-filter wegens de 1-rij-schatting). De vensterfilter staat nu als HAVING op dezelfde max-waarde, zodat alleen nog één hash-aggregate plus één join met customers op de primaire sleutel overblijft.
